 Kim A-lim Ties for Lead on First Day of LPGA Season Finale Tour Championship
 Kim Jin-u 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.20 07:58 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ Kim A-lim 
 South Korean players dominated the upper ranks on the first day of the CME Group Tour Championship (total purse $11 million), the season finale of the LPGA Tour. 
 Kim A-lim shot 7-under-par 65 with nine birdies and two bogeys in the first round of the tournament held on November 20 (Korean time) at the Tiburon Golf Club (par 72) in Naples, Florida, USA. 
 Kim, who debuted on the LPGA Tour in 2021 thanks to her victory at the 2020 major tournament, the U.S. Women's Open, tied for the lead with Thailand's Jeeno Thitikul and Australia's Karis Davidson. 
 Kim, who has three career LPGA wins, most recently won the Hilton Grand Vacations Tournament of Champions in January of last year. 
 Kim showed some ups and downs on her front nine, picking up three birdies but also carding two bogeys. 
 However, she showed great closing strength on the back nine, firing six birdies without a single bogey. 
 After finishing the first round, Kim said in an official interview, "I feel comfortable because I've played here six times. My putts went in well and my shots were good, so I was able to get into a good rhythm." 
 Tied for fourth place, one stroke behind the co-leaders, were Yoo Hae-ran, Choi Hye-jin, and Lee So-mi, who all recorded 6-under-par 66. 
 Yoo and Choi maintained a great feel for their shots, picking up six birdies without a bogey. 
 Yoo said, "When I was a rookie, I didn't do well on Florida courses. Still, I'm doing better than before lately, and I feel like I'm becoming a fan of Florida courses starting from today." 
 World No. 1 Nelly Korda (USA) finished the first day tied for 20th at 4-under-par 68 after reducing four strokes with five birdies and one bogey. 
 If Korda wins this tournament, she will earn the points required for induction into the LPGA Hall of Fame. 
 Yoo In-ah carded two bogeys but grabbed one eagle and four birdies to finish tied for 20th at 4-under-par 68, trailing the co-leading group by three strokes.
